_readme: LLM profile catalog. Callers name a TASK, never a vendor.
An entry is a chain (array), an alias (string), or an object with
max_tokens/vision. Candidates are tried in order; on any failure the
next one is used. Sampling resolves candidate -> profile -> .env global.
Keys starting with '_' are ignored, which is how you comment in JSON.
Adding a profile here requires no code change; naming one at a call site
that is missing here raises LLMUnavailableError.
_physical_chains: The three below are the real model chains. Task profiles extend them.

default.description: General-purpose reasoning over long legal text

vision.description: Multimodal calls — only anthropic, gemini, and openai qualify

_tasks: Task profiles — retune these freely; call sites never change.

parse_billing_entry.description: Parse a natural-language billing entry into structured fields

compose_welcome_email.description: Draft the first outbound email to a new lead

triage_lead_message.description: Classify an inbound lead message as spam | escalate | continue

extract_lead_issues.description: Pull the legal issues out of a lead's message

select_kb_articles.description: Choose the knowledge-base articles that answer a lead's issues

compose_lead_reply.description: Draft the substantive reply to a lead — quality over latency

response_guardrail.description: Safety check on a drafted reply before it can be sent

explain_message_edit.description: Explain how staff edited an AI draft before sending

classify_discovery_document.description: Identify discovery type, propounding party, and service dates

extract_discovery_items.description: Split a discovery document into numbered items, verbatim

extract_account_statement.description: Read a bank/brokerage/card statement into signed transactions

analyze_pleading.description: Extract case metadata, children, and counsel from a filed pleading

extract_pleading_claims.description: Extract claims, defenses, and counterclaims from a pleading

ocr_document_page.description: Read text off a scanned page image

_chain_order: Order is from measured accuracy on a hard extraction, not from price. The same 27-page, 286-transaction statement was run through each vendor by hand: Claude and OpenAI were both complete and correct; Gemini did well on what it produced but stopped after 200 entries; DeepSeek lost and mis-stated amounts and invented JSON keys, so it appears in no chain and must not be added to one that touches evidence.
_timeouts: timeout_seconds overrides the global LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS per profile. Set it where the answer is long. A deadline too short for the work does not merely fail: it selects for whichever model gives up soonest, because a short answer is the only kind that fits. On a 27-page statement at the global 90s, the run that "succeeded" returned 38 of 286 transactions, and the run where all three vendors tried to finish was killed three times. extract_account_statement gets 300s and ocr_document_page 180s; both run inside background jobs, where a generous deadline costs only patience.
